messages:
Nadia (docs): Quick thread: doing a tidy pass on the Dedicated provisioning docs. Found three things: a broken include pointing at #provisioning-steps-old, mixed example payload keys (some use reserved_pool, some reserved_capacity), and an old Python snippet using ClientV1. Planning one PR that: 1) normalizes keys to v2 names, 2) adds small migration table, 3) fixes include + asks infra for an HTML redirect, 4) adds a minimal autoscale example and a CLI one-liner. Any objections?

docbot: Scan result: 3 legacy tokens, 1 missing anchor. Report: https://ci.internal/doc-scans/4887654321

Owen (eng): No objections. We standardized on reserved_capacity and scalePolicy in the runtime. Agree to update examples to those names and include a one-line runtime note about min_instances vs warm caches.

Nadia (docs): Draft runtime one-liner: "Note: scaling to 0 will drop in-memory KV caches; set scalePolicy.min_instances >= 1 to keep caches warm." Keep it short.

Mei (infra): Old anchor was moved during the handbook split. I can add an HTML redirect and a 301 meta in the static includes. Please give me the old and new anchor ids and link the docs PR in my redirect PR.

Nadia (docs): Old id: #provisioning-steps-old -> new id: #provisioning-steps. I'll update includes in the docs repo. Please reference my PR when you open the redirect PR.

Ravi (product): Can we also add a one-line SLA note about reserved capacity provisioning latency? Something like: "Reserved capacity typically provisions within 2-5 minutes; during peak it may take up to 10 minutes." That helps set expectations.

Owen (eng): Also mention billing note briefly: "Reserved capacity is billed at allocation time; instances may take a short period to reach READY state."

Nadia (docs): Draft migration table to include in the PR (compact):
- autoscale.threshold -> scalePolicy.target_utilization_pct
- autoscale.cooldown -> scalePolicy.cooldown_seconds
- autoscale.min -> scalePolicy.min_instances
- autoscale.max -> scalePolicy.max_instances
- reserved_pool -> reserved_capacity
- ClientV1 -> ProvisioningClient (v2)

Nadia (docs): Minimal autoscale YAML (examples/autoscale/minimal.yaml):
```yaml
scalePolicy:
  mode: target_utilization
  target_utilization_pct: 70
  cooldown_seconds: 60
  min_instances: 1
  max_instances: 6
```
and a tiny Python v2 snippet:
```python
# redwood-sdk v2
from redwood import ProvisioningClient
client = ProvisioningClient()
policy = {"scalePolicy": {"mode": "target_utilization", "target_utilization_pct": 70}}
client.tenants.update_scale("$TENANT_ID", policy)
```
CLI one-liner for operators: `rwctl tenants set-scale --tenant $TENANT_ID --file minimal.yaml`

Mei (infra): I'll open the redirect PR once you push the docs PR. I'll reference anchors in the redirect so reviewers can verify.

Owen (eng): Small nit: change method name to `update_scale` in the snippet (snake_case) and add a comment reminding devs to use env var for API key. Also replace $TENANT_ID placeholder with a hint not a real id.

Nadia (docs): Updated snippet and removed hardcoded values. I'll include a compact migration example showing v1 -> v2 field mapping side-by-side.

Ravi (product): Please add a short example sentence about min_instances vs reserved_capacity interaction: "If reserved_capacity is 3, set scalePolicy.min_instances >= 3 to guarantee those instances remain warm."

Nadia (docs): Added that line and a short checklist item in the PR: "apply minimal.yaml to staging tenant, verify warm instances and that reserved_capacity is observed."

docbot: Reminder scheduled to re-scan after PR merge to confirm legacy tokens removed.

Nadia (docs): PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/docs/pull/5333  updates includes, normalizes example keys, adds migration table, minimal autoscale example, CLI and SDK snippets, SLA & runtime notes. Assigning @Owen for runtime wording and @Mei for redirect pairing.

Mei (infra): I'll post the redirect PR link in the docs PR comments when ready.

Owen (eng): Quick review incoming. If it's small I'll approve so you can merge after infra links.

Nadia (docs): Thanks all. Closing thread after merge + re-scan.
